name: textstats
description: Reads a folder of text documents and an INI/JSON settings file, tokenizes the text, counts words and n-grams, computes readability scores and writes a CSV report.
author: test-split author (Claude Opus 5.5 agent)

issues.description: The loop removes items from the list it is iterating over, so the item right after each removed stopword is skipped; two stopwords in a row leave the second one in the result.
issues.fix_hint: Build a new list with a comprehension that keeps the tokens whose lowercase form is not a stopword.

issues.description: There are len(tokens) - n + 1 windows of n tokens; the range stops one early, so the last n-gram is always missing (and two tokens give no bigram at all).
reverse=True reverses the whole key, so entries with the same count come out in reverse alphabetical order instead of alphabetical order as documented.
Document names come from the corpus index file and are joined to the corpus folder unchecked, so a name like ../secret.txt (or an absolute path) reads files outside the corpus.
issues.fix_hint: Resolve the joined path and refuse it unless it is inside the resolved corpus folder.

issues.description: config imports the report module for its column names while report imports config for Settings; the cycle only loads because the package __init__ happens to import config first.
The walk nests for / for / if / try-else / if five levels deep; the file filter and the decoding should be guard clauses or a helper.
Both Flesch functions repeat the same seven lines that split the text and compute words per sentence and syllables per word; this belongs in one helper.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: MD5 is only a checksum to spot repeated documents in a report; nothing security-related depends on it being collision resistant.
It iterates over a copy of the keys, so deleting from the dict inside the loop is safe.
